When the same notes appear multiple times on a single sheet, it creates confusion about which version is the controlling set of requirements and increases the likelihood of conflicting or inconsistent information during construction. The checklist specifically flags this as a reviewer convention deficiency. Duplicate sections should be consolidated into a single 'Austin Energy Notes' section to avoid ambiguity.

Duplicate sections create confusion about which set of notes is authoritative, may lead contractors to overlook critical requirements by assuming they appear elsewhere, and violate the principle that each set of standard notes should appear once per sheet. This duplication represents poor organization and potential non-compliance with City standards requiring a single cohesive notes section.

applicableAreas: Sheets showing electrical infrastructure (Sheet 21 Preliminary Electrical Design Plan)

Block 6 contains generic "Utility Notes" (4 items) instructing the contractor to verify existing utility locations, identify conflicts, and specify pipe materials for water and wastewater only. No note found addressing developer responsibility for conduit design and installation per Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual. The electrical design plan would be the appropriate location for this requirement if infrastructure will be developer-constructed.
findings.reasoning: AEDC 1.3.0 requires a note specifying developer responsibility for designing and constructing all conduit and related infrastructure to meet current Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual. The site plan shows preliminary electrical design with underground infrastructure routing, indicating developer involvement in electrical infrastructure installation. This note establishes clear responsibility for compliance with Austin Energy standards and for cost allocation of conductor installation. Its absence is a compliance gap.

findings.comment: Austin Energy Notes section must include a note establishing developer responsibility for conduit design and installation. Please add: 'Developer is responsible for designing and constructing all conduit and related infrastructure to meet current Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual, including installation of conductors if determined during design (prior to building permit issuance) that developer will fund conductor installation. Developer is also responsible for coordinating with other utilities to resolve conflicts. All costs for these improvements are the applicant's responsibility.'
findings.observation: The Austin Energy notes on Sheet 3 include five notes addressing tree work, easement access, erosion control, clearance maintenance, and facility relocation. None of the notes present includes developer responsibility for designing and constructing conduit infrastructure or reference to the Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual. The grouping identifies that Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows electrical routing and infrastructure, indicating that conduit infrastructure is a component of this project. No note is present establishing developer responsibility for conduit design and construction per current Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual standards.
findings.reasoning: AEDC 1.3.0 establishes basic requirements for electric distribution service, including developer-installed conduit when applicable. The required note must establish that: (1) the developer is responsible for designing and constructing conduit to meet current Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual standards, (2) the developer may be responsible for conductor installation if it is determined during design that developer funding is appropriate, (3) the developer must coordinate with other utilities to resolve conflicts, and (4) all costs are the applicant's responsibility. The current reference to 'Design Criteria Manual' (not outdated standards) is essential. Absence of this note creates ambiguity about developer responsibilities during construction.

findings.comment: The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) shows underground electric service lines and associated infrastructure designed for the project, but no note on either Sheet 3 or Sheet 21 establishes developer responsibility for conduit and related infrastructure or requires compliance with current Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual. Add a note stating: 'Developer is responsible for designing and constructing all conduit and related infrastructure to meet current Austin Energy (AE) Design Criteria Manual, including the installation of conductors if determined during the design process (prior to the issuance of the building permit) that the developer will fund the installation cost of the conductors. The Developer is also responsible for coordinating with other utilities to resolve all conflicts. All costs associated with these improvements will be the responsibility of the applicant.'
applicableAreas: Sheet 3 Austin Energy Notes and Sheet 21 Electrical Design Plan
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) clearly depicts underground electrical service with labeled 'Underground Electric Line' routing throughout the site, including transformer pads, pull boxes, electrical meters, and connections to eight buildings. This represents developer-designed and (presumably) developer-installed underground electrical infrastructure/conduit. Reviewed Sheet 3 Electric Notes (Blocks 8 and 14) and Sheet 21 Utility Notes (Block 6): Sheet 3 contains five notes but none address developer responsibility for conduit installation or infrastructure meeting Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual. Sheet 21 Utility Notes specify only contractor verification requirements for existing utilities and private water/wastewater branch materials, with no mention of electrical conduit or developer responsibility for meeting electrical design standards.
findings.reasoning: AEDC 1.3.0 establishes developer responsibilities when underground electric service is being designed and installed. When a site plan shows developer-designed underground electrical infrastructure (as evidenced by the blue Underground Electric Line routing on Sheet 21), a note must be present establishing that the developer is responsible for designing and constructing conduit and related infrastructure to meet current Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual standards, including conductor installation costs if applicable. The absence of this note leaves unclear who is responsible for the infrastructure shown and fails to establish that the design must comply with current (not outdated) Austin Energy standards.

findings.comment: Electric notes are duplicated on the same sheet. Please remove the duplicate electric notes from Sheet 3 and retain only one complete set of consolidated electric notes on the general notes sheet.

The applicant has consolidated the notes to the general notes sheet, which is correct, but then unnecessarily repeated them within the same block, which creates confusion and increases visual clutter without providing additional information. Best practice requires notes to appear once in a consolidated location.

findings.comment: Current Austin Energy contact information (phone number and department name) is not provided on the cover sheet or plan sheets. Add a contact block with Austin Energy department phone number and current contact information for coordination purposes.

The absence of contact information (phone number, department name, address) means developers and contractors cannot readily reach Austin Energy for required coordination. The presence of contact information for other city departments (Water, Fire) but not Austin Energy constitutes a deficiency in providing this required information.

findings.comment: Electric Transmission Notes are included on Sheet 3 (Block 20), but no transmission infrastructure, transmission structures, or transmission easements are shown on the site plan. applicableAreas: Austin Energy Transmission Notes on Sheet 3
findings.observation: Sheet 3 contains 'Electric Transmission Notes' (Block 20) with 16 detailed notes addressing transmission easement requirements, clearances, pre-construction meetings, barricades, and construction coordination. Examined Sheet 9 (Site Plan) using vision analysis specifically searching for transmission infrastructure. Result: No transmission towers, transmission structures, transmission poles, or transmission easement labels are shown on the site plan. The site shows only 5-foot distribution electric easements and standard overhead distribution lines (OHE notation). Facts.md confirms plat-dedicated 5-foot electric easements (distribution voltage) but lists no transmission easements or transmission structures on the property.
findings.reasoning: AEDC 1.14.0 defines transmission facilities as operating at 60kV phase-to-phase or higher and establishes that transmission-specific requirements apply only 'when transmission infrastructure is involved' or when development is within 100 feet of transmission line wires. The site plan shows no transmission infrastructure, transmission structures, or transmission easements. Including detailed transmission notes (addressing 48-hour pre-construction meetings, transmission easement road requirements, 25-foot clearance zones, and OSHA transmission safety) when no transmission infrastructure is shown or present on the plans constitutes inclusion of inapplicable notes.

findings.reasoning: The General Site Plan Notes document preface states: 'Changing the required text in your plan set will result in rejection of the application.' The grouping reinforces this requirement, stating 'Notes must use the exact wording provided in the current General Site Plan Notes document.' The four notes on Sheet 3, while addressing the correct topics, have been substantively modified with additional clauses, different word order, and supplementary text. These modifications constitute non-standard wording that deviates from the required standard text.
